chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said:
I ate with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'O maid, bring us our well-known meal.' So she brought a dish containing vinegar and oil, so we ate.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam eat with vinegar and oil according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the asceticism (zuhd) and simplicity of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), demonstrating that even basic sustenance like vinegar and oil is sufficient for spiritual and physical well-being. In Shia scholarly tradition, this narrative is often cited to validate the consumption of vinegar as a 'blessing' and to encourage moderation in diet, countering both extravagance and unnecessary deprivation. It underscores the principle that the permissibility of food is not diminished by its simplicity, provided it is consumed with gratitude.
